title: How Markets View Trump's Trade Policy at the G-20
description: Nov.27 -- Chris Hyzy, chief investment officer at Merrill Lynch and U.S. Trust, Lale Topcuoglu, senior fund manager and head of credit at JOHCM, and Peter Tchir, head of macro strategy at Academy Securities, discuss market expectations of President Donald Trump's trade talks with China's President Xi Jinping at the upcoming G-20 meeting. They speak with Bloomberg's Jonathan Ferro on "Bloomberg Markets: The Open."

asr.full_text: Lali, I want to begin with you and really get an understanding to establish what the biases in this market going into this meeting in Argentina. What is it? Look I think the markets are nervous. I think the trade has been a topical subject for a whole year. I joke I say you know I think if we played bingo with keywords or being trade side credit spreads and FedRig I think you would win throughout the entire year. IT IS NOT GOING TO HAPPEN. I THINK THE BEST OUTCOME WE CAN REALLY HOPE IS SOME SORT OF A PROMISE THAT THE TWO PARTIES WILL CONTINUE THE TALKING, AND THAT WON'T HELP THE I think the best outcome we can really hope is some sort of a promise that the two parties will continue to talking and I think that will help the ease a little bit of the pressure I think that's our best outcome, but the markets are certainly nervous. Peter I think the markets are nervous, but people are actually position slightly bullish So I think we're actually set up for more of a disappointment I think it's very unpopular to say you're hopeful something good will come out I think deep down a lot of people are positioned for something good to come out I think we're going to be disappointed I THINK IT'S VERY UNPOPULAR SAY YOU ARE HOPEFUL SOMETHING GOOD WILL COME OUT. WE ARE NOT GOING TO BACK DOWN AND THINGS LIKE THAT. THAT'S SETTING THE BAR VERY, VERY LOW. SO WE WILL SEE WHAT THE MARKET DOES TODAY. AND NOT TO TAKE ONE DAY OR THE about doing those things, either. But not the market itself. And so we will see whether China is using China talking about extra tariffs, or we're not going to back down and things like that this. We'll see what the market does today, and not to take one day or the next. When you really just think about it as said before, some kind of framework have has to come at it, this weekend. It doesn't have to be a long-term . There's no way there's a long-term solution coming out. But a short term bandaid solution to keep the markets relatively stable is very much needless. And I think you have to pay attention to what China is here for the long haul. Right? I mean. We just went through midterms. Trump is going to be up for election in 2020. We'll continue to talk and just keep the market flow. From listening to you guys, it's pretty interesting to me that your expectations are so low that all it might take is a handshake and a smile and you could get a short squeeze. Well I think we all expect to handshake and a smile that's what we get every time Trump meets a world leader in person. So I think the market is well trained to expect a little photo op, some niceness, anything less than that, I think we're in freefall probably.
